overview: Black gains space with ...d4, giving a reversed Benoni-type structure. White attacks the d4 pawn with e3 (or b4, the Anglo-Polish attack) or builds with g3 and Bg2; Black defends it with ...c5 and ...Nc6 and aims for ...e5. White has queenside play with the c- and b-pawns and Black has the central space.

white_ideas.idea: Undermine d4 with e3 and exd4, or b4 to gain queenside space.
Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, pressure d4 and play on the queenside.

black_ideas.idea: Hold the d4 pawn with ...c5, ...Nc6, ...e5 and use central space.
Develop the bishops and break with ...e5 or ...f5.

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Benoni with Black pawns on c5/d4/e5 and White play on the queenside.

character.notes: Strategic fight over the d4 pawn; the Anglo-Polish b4 push is a sharp branch.

gambit.notes: No pawn is given up in the main lines.

structure.notes: Black's d4 pawn gives a fixed asymmetric centre, not fully resolved.

approach.notes: A less common Black reply that strong players use occasionally.

level.notes: Few theory lines, but Benoni-type play needs understanding.

sublines_that_differ.name: Anglo-Polish Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: White gambits a pawn on b4 for queenside play, leading to sharper positions.

character.reason: Strategic Benoni-type battle with some tactical branches.

gambit.reason: No pawn is sacrificed in the main lines.

structure.reason: The d4 pawn is advanced but the centre can still open or lock.

approach.reason: Less common but played by strong players from time to time.

level.reason: Needs feel for Benoni-type structures and little theory.

plans.reason: Black has central space while White expands on the queenside.
